newsitem.title: USA: Canada spot domestic gas eases after plant restart.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot domestic gas eases after plant restart.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices were mostly softer Monday as an Alberta plant returned to service and NYMEX faltered, market sources said.
Spot gas at Alberta's AECO storage hub was quoted at C$1.46-1.47 per gigajoule, down from C$1.48-1.53 on Friday.
August AECO was talked at C$1.43, while September business was done equally lower at C$1.40.
NOVA Corp reported earlier today that its Grande Prairie mainline in northeastern Alberta was climbing back up to capacity, with full power expected later today.
This will mean about one billion cubic feet per day of gas returning to the Alberta market.

As a result, buyers were stepping up their storage purchases. It was estimated that about 800 mmcf of gas was injected Sunday, while more than one bcf is expected to go into storage today, a Calgary-based trader said.
At Sumas, Wash., the greater usage of gas in Alberta after the plant restart pushed prices about two cents higher to about $1.10 per million British thermal units (mmBtu).
In the East, prices at Niagara slid 10 cents to about $2.29-2.30 per mmBtu in response to an early NYMEX slump and erosion of values at the New York city-gate, sources said.
